description: Search current job postings by keyword, title, company, place, pay and date. Call list_fields for filter names. Country and employment_type accept comma-separated values or arrays. Pages return up to 50 jobs (limit, default 10), or 10 when descriptions is "full" (default 8, about as many whole descriptions as fit in one reply). Pass next_cursor as cursor for the next page. One search shows up to 250 jobs; narrow filters or use count_jobs for how many match. Default results are compact summaries (employer, title, locations, pay, dates, urls, snippet). Pass view: "full", fields, or get_job for more. descriptions: "snippet" (default) previews text; "full" returns whole descriptions. title matches one phrase in order. title_advanced and description_advanced are Boolean: an operator between every two words or groups, for example title_advanced: "(engineer OR developer) AND NOT manager" (write AND NOT, never a bare NOT after a word; keep at least one word that is not negated). sort: relevance needs q, title or description; with only title_advanced or description_advanced use updated. Each page also has total (how many jobs match, the same number count_jobs gives) and total_is_estimate (true when total is an estimate; total_margin is then the 95% range either side). total is null, with total_note saying why, when the filters are slow to count (description, description_advanced, title_advanced or q without company, near or source filters) or the count did not finish within the time the page took; then call count_jobs. One whole reply (every text part and structuredContent together) stays under about 50,000 characters. Each job lists its first 10 locations; locations_total and locations_truncated: true say when there are more. A search page that would not fit gets fewer jobs, with page_note saying so; next_cursor continues at the first job not shown, so no job is skipped and only jobs shown are counted. Only one job too big on its own is shortened (description_truncated; truncated.how_to_get_rest says where the rest is). Every error has code, message, retryable (true or false) and next_step; retryable errors also have retry_after_seconds. A call that runs past 25 seconds is stopped with query_too_broad: narrow it, do not repeat it.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from the previous result, to see the next page.

descriptions.description: snippet (default): a short preview of each description, up to 50 jobs per page. full: the whole text, up to 10 jobs per page.

fields.description: Top-level job properties as a comma-separated string or field array; job_id is always included.

country.description: One or more two-letter country codes, comma-separated or as an array (US,CA).

description_advanced.description: Boolean search of the job description. AND, OR, NOT, brackets and "quoted phrases", with an operator between every two words or groups: write nurse AND NOT manager (never nurse NOT manager), and keep at least one word that is not negated. At most 200 characters and 64 words or operators.Example: python AND (sql OR "data analysis") AND NOT intern.

employment_type.description: One or more employment type values, comma-separated or as an array.

first_seen_since.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) or ISO time; jobs we first found on or after it. For a daily check for new jobs, pass the time of the last check.

near.description: A US place to search around: a ZIP code (78701), a city with its state (Austin, TX), or latitude,longitude. Use with radius_miles.

pay_min.description: Lowest yearly pay, in pay_currency (default USD). Hourly pay is about yearly / 2,080, so $45 an hour is about 93,600.

posted_since.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) or ISO time; jobs posted on or after it.

q.description: Words matched against title and description, ranked by relevance. Every word must match; for a list of skills where any may match, use description_advanced with OR, for example python OR sql OR "data analysis".

remote.description: true is the same as work_arrangement=remote.

state.description: US state, two letters (CA) or full name.

title.description: One phrase in the job title, words in order. For words in any order or Boolean logic use title_advanced.

title_advanced.description: Boolean search of the job title, words in any order. AND, OR, NOT, brackets and "quoted phrases", with an operator between every two words or groups: write nurse AND NOT manager (never nurse NOT manager), and keep at least one word that is not negated. At most 400 characters and 64 words or operators. Example: (engineer OR developer) AND NOT manager. For one phrase in order use title.

work_arrangement.description: remote, hybrid or in_person; comma-separate several.

limit.description: Jobs per page, 1-50 (1-10 when descriptions is "full"). Default 10, or 8 with descriptions "full". 250 is a REST-only page size. A page that would not fit in one reply gets fewer jobs; next_cursor continues where it stopped.

sort.description: relevance, updated. relevance needs q, title or description; with only title_advanced or description_advanced use updated.

view.description: compact (default): one short summary per job. full: every field of every job, as the REST API returns it.

name: search_jobs
title: Search jobs
